 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners in this writ petition is seeking writ of mandamus or direction restraining the respondents from passing any resolution or order or otherwise acting on such resolution or order and restraining them from demolishing or otherwise interfering with the schedule properties or any portion thereof, without following the mandatory provisions under the National Highways Act,
1956, or the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is averred that the respondents herein have resolved to demolish the private structures constructed over the schedule property for widening of road without providing any prior notice or giving any compensation.

2. Heard learned counsel appearing for both the parties.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that due to the changed circumstances, though at the earlier point of time there was marking of the schedule property and in view of the deviations made by the concerned respondent, the petitioners do not apprehend any demolition at present.

However,
would contend that the demolition, if any of the private structures constructed over the schedule property has to be in accordance with law.
4. The statement of objections filed by respondent No.1 - National Highway Authorities would state that respondent No.1 is not a necessary party to the present proceedings.
It is stated in the statement that the said stretch has not been entrusted to the 1st respondent wherein the petition schedule property is situated.

The 1st respondent is not in charge of any development, widening,
maintenance, upgradation, construction, etc., in respect of National highway No.234 (New NH-69).

5. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the National Highway Authority would contend that as stated in para-5 of the statement of objections, the National Highway Authority has not carried out any development or widening or maintenance or upgradation or construction in pertaining to the schedule property situated at Pavagada Road, Madhugiri Town, Tumakuru district.
6. Learned High Government Court Pleader on the other hand would contend that the work is carried out by the National Highway Authority and not by the State Government.

8. The grievance of petitioner would be meted, if a direction is issued to the respondents not to dispossess or demolish any private structures without following the mandatory provisions under the National Highways Act, 1956 or the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and strictly only in due process of law.
